label: L-01
title: mintedForStable is a balance delta, not an attribution: any phUSD arriving mid-call is forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: phUSD arriving at Antimatter mid-call is swept to the caller-chosen recipient as free value. PoC: 500 phUSD injected from a stablecoin's transfer hook, annihilator walks away with 700e18 instead of 200e18.
attackPath: 1. Owner registers a stablecoin whose transfer hook can push phUSD to Antimatter.
2. Annihilator calls annihilateFrom; the hook fires inside the :220-:232 measurement window.
3. mintedForStable is a balance DELTA, never compared to minter.calculateMintAmount, and is forwarded wholesale at :237.
classification.likelihood: Low - requires a registered hook-bearing stablecoin, which no observed registration has.
classification.assumptions: A hook-bearing token is registered as a supported stablecoin.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner registration of such a token.

justification: Low. The mechanism is real and PoC'd, but every path to it runs through a token property no registered stablecoin has, and the value swept is value that had to arrive from somewhere in the first place. Not suppressed as 'weird ERC20' - the point is the asymmetry in Antimatter's own discipline: on the stablecoin side the measured-balance pattern is what makes :230 fail CLOSED, while on the phUSD side the identical pattern converts an unexpected inbound into a payout instead of a revert. Related to MR-01 (parked) and shares its mitigation with M-06/F-01.
recommendation: Compute the expected stable leg from minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) and use the balance delta only as an equality assertion, so an unexpected inbound reverts rather than paying out.

tests: test_midCallPhUSDInjectionIsForwardedToRecipient - 500e18 injected from the stable's hook; annihilator receives 700e18
test_preExistingPhUSDDonationIsNotSwept - control: a pre-call 500e18 donation is correctly excluded by the :220 snapshot and remains stuck (rescueERC20-able)
test_midCallPhUSDInjectionIsForwardedToRecipient - 500e18 injected from the stable's hook; annihilator receives 700e18
test_preExistingPhUSDDonationIsNotSwept - control: a pre-call 500e18 donation is correctly excluded by the :220 snapshot and remains stuck (rescueERC20-able)

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: mintedForStable is measured as a balance delta over :220-:232 and forwarded wholesale at :237, never compared against what PhusdStableMinter actually minted (obtainable exactly via minter.calculateMintAmount). On the stablecoin side the measured-balance pattern is what makes :230 fail closed; on the phUSD side the same pattern converts an unexpected inbound into free value instead of a revert.
additionalContext.impact: A registered `stable` whose transfer hook pushes phUSD to Antimatter causes that phUSD to be swept to the annihilator. PoC: 500 phUSD injected from the token's hook, annihilator walks away with 700e18 instead of 200e18.
additionalContext.whyLow: The only non-trusted code executing inside the window is the stablecoin's own transfer path at :222, and `stable` must be owner-registered with the minter. The realistic registered set (USDC, DOLA) has no transfer hooks. The residual concern is a future registration of a hook-bearing or upgradeable stablecoin.

mergeAction: CODE-004 and AM-LOCAL-004 consolidated (identical defect, identical line :232, identical recommendation; CODE-004 adds the reproducing PoC and the control test). NOT collapsed into DEDUP-007 despite the shared :233/:232 lines and shared mitigation - different root cause (an inbound during the window is swept as free value, vs an upstream under-credit) and a different, independently reachable attack vector.
